screens.name: Home — omen loading, available, unavailable and policy expanded
screens.evidence: Sheets 39–40, 61–70, 82 and 96 show both text sizes and browser variants, with supplied runtime evidence confirming policy reachability and durable attempt handling.
findings: Explain the consumed omen attempt beside the unavailable message rather than requiring expansion of “Next: tomorrow.”

screens.name: Question entry choice
screens.evidence: Sheets 22, 71 and 82 show a dominant orb, explicit typing and speaking actions, and consistent settled and transition layouts.
findings: Retain the clear input choice and verify its spoken labels and focus order on the physical device.

screens.name: Question composer — self, named person and constrained viewport
screens.evidence: Sheets 12, 22–24, 72–73 and 83 show composer variants, while supplied runtime evidence confirms draft retention and submission only through Ask.
findings: Shorten the persistent disclosure so enlarged-text users reach their question with less scrolling.

screens.name: Named-person selection
screens.evidence: Sheets 23–24 show the Someone selection, labeled name field, explicit confirmation and privacy explanation at normal and enlarged text.
findings: Keep cancellation easy to discover when the enlarged name form pushes it below the initial viewport.

screens.name: Voice entry — unavailable and retry
screens.evidence: Sheets 40–41 and 82 show a readable failure explanation, typing fallback and voice retry, with actual speech explicitly unverified.
findings: Verify microphone denial and successful dictation on-device before treating the voice path as dependable.

screens.name: Follow-up questions — initial steps and disabled progression
screens.evidence: Sheets 25–27 and 85 show numbered steps, unselected radios and disabled Continue or Reveal, supported by measured targets and browser keyboard checks.
findings: Keep mist contrast consistently subdued behind the question and option rows.

screens.name: Follow-up questions — selected, keyboard focused and final answer
screens.evidence: Sheets 3–5, 28 and 86 show selected radio marks, visible focus and enabled progression across text sizes and motion variants.
findings: Preserve the separate selection and Continue or Reveal steps.

screens.name: Custom answer — empty, populated, long and constrained
screens.evidence: Sheets 27 and 72 show labeled custom answers, disabled empty-state progression and reachable Reveal in constrained views.
findings: Make the distinction between returning to choices and returning to the previous question clearer.

screens.name: Expanded question editor — all represented widths and heights
screens.evidence: Sheets 19–21 show persistent Cancel and Done around a scrollable editor, and supplied runtime evidence reports complete drafts and restored focus across the viewport matrix.
findings: Retain persistent editor controls and recheck caret visibility with the native keyboard.

screens.name: Expanded custom-answer editor — all represented widths and heights
screens.evidence: Sheets 16–18 show the retained question label and large scrollable answer field, supported by repeated Cancel, Done and immediate re-edit regression checks.
findings: Provide a clearer scroll cue when enlarged text opens midway through a long answer.

screens.name: AI permission — review entry, disclosure and decision
screens.evidence: Sheets 14–15 show permission review and grant or decline controls, with supplied temporary-preview checks establishing no generation request during permission actions.
findings: State the permission’s scope in one concise summary before the detailed data categories.

screens.name: Planning and research — initial loading and extended wait
screens.evidence: Sheets 47–48, 83 and 86 show distinct planning and research descriptions, a long-wait update and cancellation, supported by timeout and motion evidence.
findings: Keep the factual stage description more prominent than the repeated atmospheric loading headline.

screens.name: Forecast failure — planning, prediction and timeout
screens.evidence: Sheets 33–34, 84 and 86 show retry, editing, applicable answer review and a timeout message, with supplied evidence confirming retained answers and no spending.
findings: Include the no-reading-spent reassurance in the generic connection failure as consistently as in the timeout state.

screens.name: Sensitive-question redirect — support and general variants
screens.evidence: Sheets 52–53 and 84 show a support-link variant and a general redirect with alternate-question and editing routes.
findings: Lead with the humane explanation of why the question needs care before the branded rejection headline.

screens.name: Forecast opening — normal, golden, skip and reduced motion
screens.evidence: Sheets 73–78 show orb-to-forecast continuity and settled variants, with supplied runtime evidence covering skip, interruption, early sharing and reduced-motion behavior.
findings: Give “Show forecast” stronger visual prominence during the opening so the skip route is immediately apparent.

screens.name: Forecast reveal — settled and More actions expanded
screens.evidence: Sheets 49–51 and 73–78 show the forecast, uncertainty label, reminder and expandable actions across enlarged, transition and settled states.
findings: Label the small replay orb explicitly if it is actionable; its purpose is not visually self-evident.

screens.name: Free explanation — recorded context, assumption and limits
screens.evidence: Sheets 5–6 and 83 show separated context, assumption and limits with forecast return and an upgrade boundary.
findings: Place recorded context ahead of the playful Sun-sign introduction to make the explanation’s basis easier to scan.

screens.name: Reading details — section index
screens.evidence: Sheets 13 and 49–50 show a single-column four-section index, with supplied runtime evidence confirming focus restoration on return.
findings: Differentiate “Read the forecast” from “Back to forecast” or consolidate their overlapping navigation roles.

screens.name: Reading details — answers reader
screens.evidence: Sheets 11, 34–35 show long answer content and question labels, with supplied runtime evidence establishing complete stored text and return controls.
findings: Reduce the repeated reader header stack so enlarged-text users reach the answer sooner.

screens.name: Reading details — assumptions reader
screens.evidence: Sheets 12 and 35–36 show the assumptions reader with top and bottom navigation, including long synthetic text.
findings: Consolidate the bottom section-return and forecast-return choices into clearly distinct destinations.

screens.name: Reading details — legacy reason reader and direct explanation
screens.evidence: Sheets 13, 36 and 51 show numbered passages and a saved-explanation introduction, supported by complete-text and focus-return evidence.

screens.name: Reading details — background sources reader
screens.evidence: Sheets 14 and 37 show source titles, dates, summaries and external actions beneath an explicit background-only disclaimer.
findings: Move each source’s open action closer to its title so long summaries do not bury the destination.

screens.name: Check-in — initial, selected unsaved and saved outcomes
screens.evidence: Sheets 28–31 and 78–81 show all three saved outcomes and unsaved states, backed by persistence, correction and reload checks.

screens.name: Check-in — forecast and additional actions expanded
screens.evidence: Sheets 28–30 and 78–82 show expanded forecast and action groups below the outcome form at both text sizes.

screens.name: History — empty
screens.evidence: Sheets 38–39 show the empty-history message, local-storage label and Ask the Ball route at both text sizes.
findings: Give the sole empty-state action a stronger affordance than an ordinary text link.

screens.name: History — populated
screens.evidence: Sheets 37–38 and 85 show dated questions, forecasts, reminders and check-in links, supported by reload evidence.

screens.name: Sky — sample stars, selected question and offline fallback
screens.evidence: Sheets 56–57 and 85 show star selection, the enlarged-text grid, a selected sample question and an explicitly offline variant.

screens.name: Circles — unavailable and failed retry
screens.evidence: Sheets 11 and 31–33 show honest unavailable and retry-failed states, while supplied runtime evidence states that Supabase is unconfigured.

screens.name: Onboarding — age confirmation
screens.evidence: Sheets 41–42 show explicit age choices and explain that skipping a birthday applies the younger age limits.

screens.name: Onboarding — optional birthday and correction form

limitations: Scores are provisional browser judgments based on the supplied screenshots and runtime account; I did not independently execute the reported checks.
Dimension scores use the full browser range under the stage clarification; a browser 9 does not certify native or physical assistive-technology quality.
For each entry, A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility; overall is 0.4A + 0.6F, excluding genuinely inapplicable null dimensions.

Corresponding transitions and repeated viewport variants are grouped with their settled screen; static frames establish visible continuity but not animation behavior independently of the supplied runtime evidence.
Below-fold content and internally scrolled text are not classified as inaccessible solely because a screenshot cuts them off.
No current browser hard-gate failure is established by this material; reported resolution of the editor data-loss regression is accepted provisionally rather than independently reproduced.
Circles receives an offline-state grade only; authenticated social functionality is unavailable and cannot receive a completed-task grade.
Voice, OS sharing, clipboard delivery, native notifications, real payments, physical keyboard behavior, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver remain unverified boundaries.
Synthetic predictions, repetitive reader fixtures, test-provider labels and simulated plans are not treated as production-copy defects or evidence of predictive quality.
The screenshot deck predates the stated final focus-callback change; identical composition and fresh focus verification are supplied assertions.
Contrast, target-size, frame-time and axe results support the browser assessment but do not establish novice usability or audible assistive-technology behavior.
The requested A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met across all screens and components.
topFixes: Simplify reading-detail navigation: reduce repeated headers and distinguish section return, forecast expansion and forecast return.
Explain the consumed omen attempt directly in the unavailable state.
Improve enlarged-text information order so chart inputs, history actions and reader content remain close to their relevant controls.
Make result wording precise: cancellation is neutral, reminder preview schedules nothing, and dismissing export preparation needs a clear meaning.
Expose the selectable invitation URL immediately after copy failure.
Give the opening skip action and any actionable small replay orb explicit, readily discoverable labels.
